path.name: Your Own YouTube Channel
path.tagline: Build a channel around one audience and publish your way to your first channel income.
path.description: You pick one audience, learn what they search for, and publish videos that answer it, using only a phone and free tools. Over 30 days you build a repeatable process for ideas, recording, editing and packaging, then read your analytics to improve each upload. Income on your own channel builds slowly, so the goal is a working system, real audience signal and one honest first income attempt.
path.objective: Publish consistently for 30 days, build a repeatable production process, learn from your analytics and make one stage-appropriate first income attempt, such as an affiliate link for a product you really use.
path.typicalPrice: Affiliate and sponsor income first; ads come later
firstTasks: Write down who your channel is for and the problem it helps them with
Set up your channel name, profile picture, banner and About text
Collect 20 video ideas from search autocomplete and comments on similar channels
Script, record and publish your first video by Day 12
workflow: Pick a topic from your idea bank that your audience is already searching for
Write a short script with a strong hook, a clear promise and one call to action
Record on your phone with good light and clear audio
Edit in a free editor, cutting pauses and adding simple captions
Package it with a clear title and a readable thumbnail, then publish
Reply to comments and turn one section into a Short
Review analytics weekly and feed what you learn into the next video

tools.name: YouTube Studio
tools.purpose: Upload, schedule, reply to comments and read analytics

tools.name: CapCut
tools.purpose: Edit long-form videos and Shorts on your phone or computer

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve
tools.purpose: Edit long-form videos on a computer with more control

tools.name: Canva
tools.purpose: Design thumbnails, your banner and a simple media kit

tools.name: Google Trends
tools.purpose: Compare topic interest over time, with a YouTube Search filter

tools.name: Google Docs
tools.purpose: Write scripts and keep your idea bank in one place

plan.missionTitle: Decide who your channel is for and what it helps them do.
plan.goal: Write a one-sentence channel promise and your 30-day goal.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 1 lesson
tasks.description: See how an owned channel grows: one audience, one problem, steady uploads and patient learning from your analytics.

tasks.title: Name your audience
tasks.description: Write who you want to help in plain words. Be specific enough that one person could read it and think "that is me".

tasks.title: Write your channel promise
tasks.description: Use this shape: "I help [audience] with [problem] through [type of video]." Keep it to one sentence.

tasks.title: Set your 30-day goal
tasks.description: Choose a process goal you control, such as "publish 6 videos and 6 Shorts". View counts are not in your control yet.

tasks.title: Block your daily slot
tasks.description: Pick a fixed 30 to 60 minute slot for the next 30 days and put it in your calendar.

plan.nicheHint: Draft your promise as: I help {audience} with {problem} through {niche} videos. If it feels too broad, narrow the audience before you narrow the topic.

stageHints.idea: Write your promise from scratch and pick the audience you understand best.
stageHints.started: Read your existing uploads and write the promise that best describes the videos that already got a reaction.
stageHints.some_traction: Check which videos bring most of your viewers and make sure your promise matches them.
stageHints.already_earning: Write the promise around the audience that already pays attention, and note which videos led to income.

plan.missionTitle: Set up a clean channel that tells a new viewer what it is about in five seconds.
plan.goal: Finish your name, profile picture, banner and About section.

tasks.title: Choose a channel name
tasks.description: Pick something short, easy to spell and easy to say out loud. Your own name plus a topic word works well.

tasks.title: Create a profile picture and banner
tasks.description: Use Canva's free YouTube banner size. Put your promise on the banner in large text that reads on a phone.

tasks.title: Write your About section
tasks.description: Two or three sentences: who it is for, what they will learn and how often you upload.

tasks.title: Check it on your phone
tasks.description: Open your channel in the YouTube app. If the banner text is hard to read, make it bigger.

plan.nicheHint: Put your promise for {audience} on the banner and use one or two of these words in your About text: {terms}.

stageHints.idea: Create the channel today using the checklist; it takes less than an hour.
stageHints.started: Refresh your banner and About text so they match the promise you wrote on Day 1.
stageHints.some_traction: Update your banner and About text to reflect what your best-performing videos are about.
stageHints.already_earning: Add a short line in your About text about who to contact for brand partnerships and check your links work.

plan.missionTitle: Find out what your audience types into search and asks in comments.
plan.goal: Collect 15 real questions your audience is asking.

tasks.title: Use search autocomplete
tasks.description: Type your topic into the YouTube search bar, then add words like "how to", "why", "best" and each letter of the alphabet. Save the suggestions.

tasks.title: Read comments on similar channels
tasks.description: Open five recent videos from channels near your size in your topic. Copy questions and complaints viewers leave in the comments.

tasks.title: Note the exact words
tasks.description: Write questions in the viewer's words, not yours. These words become your titles later.

tasks.title: Highlight repeat questions
tasks.description: Mark any question you saw more than once. Repeat questions are your strongest topics.

plan.nicheHint: Search for {terms} and look for questions from {audience} about {problem}. Save at least 15 in their exact wording.

stageHints.idea: Do the full research from scratch; this is the base for your first ten videos.
stageHints.started: Compare what you find to your existing uploads and note the questions you have not answered yet.
stageHints.some_traction: Look for follow-up questions in your own comments as well as on similar channels.
stageHints.already_earning: Add a column for questions that hint at a product or tool your viewers want help choosing.

plan.missionTitle: Use Google Trends to see which of your topics hold steady interest.
plan.goal: Pick five strong topics from your research.

tasks.title: Open Google Trends
tasks.description: Set the search filter to YouTube Search and the time range to the past 12 months.

tasks.title: Compare your topics
tasks.description: Enter up to five topic phrases from yesterday's list and compare them. Note which ones are steady, rising or seasonal.

tasks.title: Score each topic
tasks.description: Give each topic a score out of 3 for interest, your knowledge and how easy it is to film with what you have.

tasks.title: Choose your top five
tasks.description: Keep the five highest-scoring topics. These are the pillars your first videos come from.

plan.nicheHint: Compare phrases like {terms} in Google Trends. Prefer topics where {audience} keeps searching all year over short spikes.

stageHints.idea: Choose topics you can film at home this month with a phone.
stageHints.started: Check whether your best existing video sits on a steady topic and plan more around it.
stageHints.some_traction: Look for seasonal peaks coming up in the next two months and plan to publish before them.
stageHints.already_earning: Favor topics where viewers are deciding what to buy or use, since those suit affiliate links later.

plan.missionTitle: Turn your research into 20 specific video ideas.
plan.goal: Fill your idea bank with 20 ideas, each with a working title.

tasks.title: Open the idea bank template
tasks.description: Copy it into Google Docs or Sheets so you can add to it every week.

tasks.title: Write 20 ideas
tasks.description: Each idea answers one question for one viewer. "Beginner mistakes" is a topic; "5 mistakes that make your first week harder" is an idea.

tasks.title: Give each a working title
tasks.description: Write the title a viewer would click. It will change later, but it keeps the idea focused.

tasks.title: Mark your first three
tasks.description: Pick three ideas that are easy to film and answer a repeat question. These are videos 1, 2 and 3.

plan.nicheHint: Write ideas that solve one part of {problem} for {audience}. Use the words people search, like {terms}, in the working titles.

stageHints.idea: Aim for 20 ideas now so you never start a recording day without a topic.
stageHints.started: Add 20 new ideas and mark any old upload worth remaking with better packaging.
stageHints.some_traction: Build at least five ideas as follow-ups to your best-performing videos.
stageHints.already_earning: Include a few ideas that compare or review tools your audience asks about.

plan.missionTitle: Decide between long-form, Shorts or both based on your time and equipment.
plan.goal: Commit to one format plan for the next three weeks.

tasks.title: Count your real weekly hours
tasks.description: Be honest. A simple long-form video can take several hours for a beginner; a Short takes less.

tasks.title: Check your equipment
tasks.description: A phone, a quiet room and a window are enough. Note what you have, not what you wish you had.

tasks.title: Pick your format plan
tasks.description: Low time: Shorts plus one long video every two weeks. More time: one long video a week plus two Shorts cut from it.

tasks.title: Watch three examples
tasks.description: Find three videos in your format from small channels and note their length, pacing and style.

plan.nicheHint: Look at how small channels serving {audience} use long-form and Shorts, then choose the mix you can keep up in {niche}.

stageHints.idea: Start with the simplest plan you can repeat, even if it feels small.
stageHints.started: Look at which format your uploads did better in and lean into it.
stageHints.some_traction: Keep your main format and add the other as a support, such as Shorts that point to long videos.
stageHints.already_earning: Protect the format that earns and test the second format only if your schedule has room.

plan.missionTitle: Turn your first idea into a simple outline you can film.
plan.goal: Finish a one-page outline for video 1.

tasks.title: Review your week
tasks.description: Reread your promise, research and idea bank. Make sure video 1 fits the promise.

tasks.title: Outline the video
tasks.description: Write three to five key points in the order a beginner needs them.

tasks.title: Decide the one takeaway
tasks.description: Write the one thing a viewer should remember. Everything in the video supports it.

tasks.title: Schedule filming
tasks.description: Put a recording slot for Day 9 in your calendar now.

plan.nicheHint: Outline a video that helps {audience} with one specific part of {problem}, not the whole thing.

stageHints.idea: Choose the easiest idea from your top three so you finish it.
stageHints.started: Choose an idea that answers a question your current viewers already asked.
stageHints.some_traction: Plan a follow-up to your best video so returning viewers have a reason to click.
stageHints.already_earning: Plan a video where a tool or product you really use fits naturally, without forcing it.

plan.missionTitle: Write the script for your first video, starting with a strong hook.
plan.goal: Finish a full script with hook, promise, content and call to action.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 8 lesson
tasks.description: Learn why the first 15 to 30 seconds decide whether people stay.

tasks.title: Write three hooks
tasks.description: Try a question, a surprising result and a common mistake. Pick the one you would click.

tasks.title: Write the promise line
tasks.description: Tell the viewer what they will get by the end. One sentence.

tasks.title: Write the main content
tasks.description: Turn your outline into short spoken sentences. Read it out loud and cut anything you stumble on.

tasks.title: Add one call to action
tasks.description: Ask for one thing only, such as watching a related video or leaving a question in the comments.

plan.nicheHint: Open with the problem {audience} feels most, in their words, then promise a clear result tied to {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Write a full script for video 1; it removes most of the stress on recording day.
stageHints.started: Compare your new hook to the openings of your older uploads and note what changed.
stageHints.some_traction: Check where viewers dropped off in your top video and write a hook that avoids that early slowdown.
stageHints.already_earning: Write the script so any product mention comes after the viewer already got value.

plan.missionTitle: Record your first video on your phone with good light and clear sound.
plan.goal: Get usable footage of the full script.

tasks.title: Set up your light
tasks.description: Face a window during the day. Avoid having a bright window behind you.

tasks.title: Fix your audio
tasks.description: Record in the quietest, softest room you have. Close windows and get close to the phone, or use wired earphones with a mic.

tasks.title: Do a 20-second test
tasks.description: Record a test, play it back with headphones and fix light or sound before the full take.

tasks.title: Record in short sections
tasks.description: Record one point at a time. If you trip on a line, pause and say it again; you will cut it later.

plan.nicheHint: Film a setup that suits {niche}: a talking head, hands-on demo or screen recording, whichever shows the solution to {problem} best.

stageHints.idea: Record with your phone as it is; good light and sound matter more than the camera.
stageHints.started: Watch one old upload and fix the single biggest light or sound issue before filming.
stageHints.some_traction: Record an extra 30 seconds of b-roll so editing feels more dynamic.
stageHints.already_earning: Batch-record the intro for two videos while your setup is ready.

plan.missionTitle: Edit your first video in a free editor.
plan.goal: Export a finished first cut.

tasks.title: Import and cut
tasks.description: Bring your footage into CapCut or DaVinci Resolve. Cut silences, mistakes and repeated lines.

tasks.title: Tighten the opening
tasks.description: Make sure the hook starts in the first seconds with no greeting before it.

tasks.title: Add simple text and captions
tasks.description: Use auto captions, then fix any wrong words. Keep text short and readable on a phone.

tasks.title: Check audio levels
tasks.description: Your voice should be clear and steady. Keep any music quiet and use only music you have the right to use.

tasks.title: Export
tasks.description: Export at the resolution you recorded in. Save the project file in case you need changes.

plan.nicheHint: Add on-screen text for key terms like {terms} so viewers who watch without sound still follow.

stageHints.idea: Aim for done, not perfect; your edit skills grow with every video.
stageHints.started: Edit faster than last time by cutting pauses first and adding extras last.
stageHints.some_traction: Add pattern changes, like a zoom or b-roll, near the spots where viewers dropped before.
stageHints.already_earning: Set up a reusable project template so edits take less time each week.

plan.missionTitle: Package your first video so the right viewers want to click.
plan.goal: Choose a final title and design one thumbnail.

tasks.title: Write ten titles
tasks.description: Write ten options using your audience's words. Keep the strongest one clear before clever.

tasks.title: Sketch the thumbnail idea
tasks.description: One subject, one feeling, and three words or fewer of text.

tasks.title: Design it in Canva
tasks.description: Use the YouTube thumbnail size, big contrast and a face or a clear object. Check it at phone size.

tasks.title: Test it next to others
tasks.description: Place your thumbnail next to search results for your topic. If it disappears, simplify it.

plan.nicheHint: Write titles that name the result {audience} wants and use one search phrase from {terms}.

stageHints.idea: Spend real time here; packaging decides whether anyone sees your first video.
stageHints.started: Write a new title and thumbnail for your weakest old upload while you are at it.
stageHints.some_traction: Compare your best and worst click-through rate videos and copy what the best one does.
stageHints.already_earning: Keep thumbnails honest; trust matters more once viewers rely on your recommendations.

plan.missionTitle: Upload and publish your first video.
plan.goal: Video 1 is live on your channel.

tasks.title: Upload in YouTube Studio
tasks.description: Add your title, thumbnail and a description whose first two lines say what the viewer will learn.

tasks.title: Add chapters and an end screen
tasks.description: Add timestamps in the description for chapters and an end screen pointing to your channel or another video.

tasks.title: Choose the right settings
tasks.description: Set the audience setting honestly, add a few relevant tags and pick a category.

tasks.title: Publish and share once
tasks.description: Publish, then share it with one group or person who would genuinely find it useful.

plan.nicheHint: In the description, explain in plain words how the video helps {audience} with {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Publish today even if it feels unfinished; the first upload teaches you more than any lesson.
stageHints.started: Publish and compare the first 48 hours to your past uploads, not to other channels.
stageHints.some_traction: Publish at the time your audience is most active, shown in YouTube Studio analytics.
stageHints.already_earning: Publish and pin a comment that points to your most useful resource for this topic.

plan.missionTitle: Choose a publishing schedule you can keep for months, not days.
plan.goal: A written schedule with dates for the next three uploads.

tasks.title: Look at your real time
tasks.description: Use how long video 1 took to estimate each upload. Most beginners underestimate by a lot.

tasks.title: Pick a cadence
tasks.description: One long video a week, or one every two weeks plus Shorts. Consistent beats frequent.

tasks.title: Put dates in your calendar
tasks.description: Block script, record, edit and publish days for the next three uploads.

tasks.title: Tell your viewers
tasks.description: Add your upload rhythm to your About section or banner.

plan.nicheHint: Choose a rhythm that fits {niche} and your week; {audience} will come back more for reliable uploads than for sudden bursts.

stageHints.idea: Pick the slowest schedule you could keep even in a busy week.
stageHints.started: Restart with a schedule you can keep, even if you posted irregularly before.
stageHints.some_traction: Hold your current cadence and add Shorts only if your schedule allows it.
stageHints.already_earning: Keep the cadence steady and plan which uploads will include partner or affiliate mentions.

plan.missionTitle: Script, record, edit and publish your second video.
plan.goal: Video 2 is live.

tasks.title: Pick video 2 from your idea bank
tasks.description: Choose one of the three ideas you marked on Day 5.

tasks.title: Script and record
tasks.description: Use the same template and setup. It should feel faster than last time.

tasks.title: Edit and package
tasks.description: Edit, then write titles and a thumbnail using the checklist.

tasks.title: Publish and link
tasks.description: Publish it and add an end screen that points to video 1.

plan.nicheHint: Make video 2 a close neighbor of video 1 so viewers interested in {problem} have a next video to watch.

stageHints.idea: Finish and publish; two videos make your channel look active to new visitors.
stageHints.started: Publish and note which step took longest so you can fix it next week.
stageHints.some_traction: Publish a follow-up to your best video and link the two with end screens.
stageHints.already_earning: Publish and check that every affiliate or partner link in older descriptions still works.

plan.missionTitle: Cut Shorts from your long videos that make viewers want the full version.
plan.goal: Publish two Shorts cut from your videos.

tasks.title: Find two strong moments
tasks.description: Look for a tip, a surprising line or a quick result in videos 1 and 2.

tasks.title: Reframe to vertical
tasks.description: Use CapCut to crop to vertical, add captions and start on the strongest sentence.

tasks.title: Link to the full video
tasks.description: Use the related video option in the Shorts upload so viewers can jump to the long version.

tasks.title: Publish both Shorts
tasks.description: Publish one today and schedule one for later this week.

plan.nicheHint: Pick moments where {audience} gets one quick win on {problem}, and use a search phrase like {terms} in the Short's title.

stageHints.idea: If you only have one video, make two Shorts from it.
stageHints.started: Turn your best older section into a Short and link it to the full video.
stageHints.some_traction: Make Shorts from your top retention moments, shown in the retention graph.
stageHints.already_earning: Use Shorts to point to the videos where your affiliate or product links live.

plan.missionTitle: Turn viewers into a community by replying and starting conversations.
plan.goal: Reply to every comment and pin a question on each video.

tasks.title: Reply to every comment
tasks.description: Thank people by name and answer questions fully. Early replies show viewers there is a real person here.

tasks.title: Pin a question
tasks.description: Pin a comment on each video that asks viewers about their own situation.

tasks.title: Collect new ideas
tasks.description: Copy any question from comments into your idea bank.

tasks.title: Check the Community tab
tasks.description: If it is available on your channel, post a simple poll asking what viewers want next.

plan.nicheHint: Pin a question that invites {audience} to share where they are stuck with {problem}.

stageHints.idea: If you have no comments yet, leave thoughtful comments on similar small channels as a viewer, not as an ad.
stageHints.started: Reply to every comment, including old ones you missed.
stageHints.some_traction: Heart and reply to comments from returning viewers to make them feel seen.
stageHints.already_earning: Ask viewers which tools or products they want you to review next.

plan.missionTitle: Script and record your third video in one session.
plan.goal: Video 3 script and footage are done.

tasks.title: Choose the topic
tasks.description: Pick the idea that came up most in comments or research.

tasks.title: Write the script
tasks.description: Try a different hook style than videos 1 and 2.

tasks.title: Record
tasks.description: Use your recording checklist and record in sections.

tasks.title: Note what was easier
tasks.description: Write one thing that got easier and one thing that still slows you down.

plan.nicheHint: Answer the most repeated question from {audience} about {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Keep using the same setup; consistency in setup saves time.
stageHints.started: Try one upgrade, such as a better angle or cleaner background.
stageHints.some_traction: Record a longer, deeper video on your strongest topic.
stageHints.already_earning: Record an honest review or tutorial of a tool you use, focused on viewer value.

plan.missionTitle: Edit, package and publish your third video.
plan.goal: Video 3 is live with a pinned comment.

tasks.title: Edit
tasks.description: Cut pauses first, then add captions and simple text.

tasks.title: Package
tasks.description: Write ten titles and design one thumbnail.

tasks.title: Publish
tasks.description: Add chapters, an end screen and a pinned question.

tasks.title: Update older videos
tasks.description: Add an end screen or card on videos 1 and 2 pointing to video 3.

plan.nicheHint: Use a title that names the result {audience} wants and includes a phrase from {terms}.

stageHints.idea: Publish; three videos give viewers a reason to subscribe.
stageHints.started: Publish and check that all your videos now link to each other.
stageHints.some_traction: Publish and create a playlist around this topic.
stageHints.already_earning: Publish and review your description template so disclosures and links are consistent.

plan.missionTitle: Review your first analytics and learn what they are telling you.
plan.goal: Write three insights from YouTube Studio.

tasks.title: Open YouTube Studio analytics
tasks.description: Look at the Content tab for each video.

tasks.title: Check click-through rate
tasks.description: Impressions click-through rate shows how often people who saw your thumbnail clicked. Compare your own videos to each other.

tasks.title: Check average view duration and retention
tasks.description: Find where viewers leave. A sharp early drop usually means the hook or opening is slow.

tasks.title: Check traffic sources and returning viewers
tasks.description: See whether views came from search, browse, Shorts or external links, and how many viewers came back.

tasks.title: Write three insights
tasks.description: One about packaging, one about retention, one about where viewers come from.

plan.nicheHint: Ask which video made {audience} stay longest and which topic around {problem} got the most clicks.

stageHints.idea: If you have very few views, focus on retention; small numbers still show where people leave.
stageHints.started: Compare your three newest videos to your older ones.
stageHints.some_traction: Look at returning viewers and the videos that bring them back.
stageHints.already_earning: Compare which videos drive clicks on your links, not only views.

plan.missionTitle: Use what you learned to improve the title or thumbnail of one video.
plan.goal: Update packaging on your weakest video.

tasks.title: Pick the weakest video
tasks.description: Choose the one with the lowest click-through rate or impressions that are not turning into views.

tasks.title: Write a new title
tasks.description: Make the benefit clearer or add the search phrase viewers use.

tasks.title: Make a new thumbnail
tasks.description: Simplify it: fewer words, bigger subject, stronger contrast.

tasks.title: Log the change
tasks.description: Note the date and the old numbers so you can compare in a week.

plan.nicheHint: Make the benefit for {audience} obvious in under three words on the thumbnail.

stageHints.idea: If you have only one or two videos, practice by redesigning a thumbnail and keeping the better one.
stageHints.started: Update the packaging on your weakest upload and compare in a week.
stageHints.some_traction: Use YouTube Studio's thumbnail testing if it is available to you, or change one element at a time.
stageHints.already_earning: Improve packaging on videos that already earn so more viewers see them.

plan.missionTitle: Script and record two videos in one session to stay ahead.
plan.goal: Two scripts done and at least one video recorded.

tasks.title: Pick two ideas
tasks.description: Choose two related ideas so research overlaps.

tasks.title: Write both scripts
tasks.description: Write both hooks first, then both bodies.

tasks.title: Record both
tasks.description: Change your shirt or angle between them if you want them to feel different.

tasks.title: Schedule publish dates
tasks.description: Add both to your publishing planner.

plan.nicheHint: Batch two related videos for {audience}, such as a beginner and a next-step video about {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Batch just two scripts if recording two in one day is too much.
stageHints.started: Batch two videos so next week does not depend on a perfect day.
stageHints.some_traction: Batch three videos and plan Shorts from each.
stageHints.already_earning: Batch videos around the topics that earn and schedule them ahead.

plan.missionTitle: Publish your batched video and the Shorts cut from it.
plan.goal: Video 4 and one Short are live.

tasks.title: Edit the batched video
tasks.description: Edit using your project template.

tasks.title: Package and publish
tasks.description: Use the packaging checklist, then publish on your planned date.

tasks.title: Cut one Short
tasks.description: Turn the best moment into a Short linked to the full video.

tasks.title: Reply to comments
tasks.description: Reply to every comment within a day.

plan.nicheHint: Use a Short to give {audience} one quick win, then point them to the full video on {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Publish; four uploads in one month is a real foundation.
stageHints.started: Publish and notice how much faster this one went.
stageHints.some_traction: Publish and add the video to a playlist so viewers keep watching.
stageHints.already_earning: Publish and include any relevant affiliate links with clear disclosure.

plan.missionTitle: Learn the realistic income options for your channel's stage.
plan.goal: Pick one first income attempt for this month.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 23 lesson
tasks.description: See the order income usually arrives on an owned channel: affiliate links and small sponsorships often come before ad revenue.

tasks.title: Check YouTube Partner Program eligibility
tasks.description: Open YouTube Studio > Earn and read the current eligibility requirements. Do not rely on numbers you heard elsewhere; they change.

tasks.title: List what you already use
tasks.description: Write down products and tools you genuinely use and would recommend.

tasks.title: Pick one first attempt
tasks.description: Choose one: an affiliate link, a sponsorship-ready media kit or validating a digital product idea.

plan.nicheHint: List tools or products that genuinely help {audience} with {problem}. Only include things you have used yourself.

stageHints.idea: Write the plan only; publishing and learning come before income at this stage.
stageHints.started: Pick one affiliate product you already use and plan where it fits.
stageHints.some_traction: Check YouTube Studio > Earn and prepare a simple media kit.
stageHints.already_earning: Review which income source works best and pick one new one to test.

plan.missionTitle: Set up one affiliate link with proper disclosure.
plan.goal: One affiliate link added with a clear disclosure.

tasks.title: Find an affiliate program
tasks.description: Check if a product you use has an affiliate program and read its rules.

tasks.title: Write your disclosure
tasks.description: Add a plain disclosure near the link, such as "This is an affiliate link. I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you."

tasks.title: Turn on the paid promotion setting when it applies
tasks.description: If a video includes paid promotion, tick the paid promotion box in the upload settings.

tasks.title: Add the link to a relevant video
tasks.description: Put it only on a video where it genuinely helps the viewer.

plan.nicheHint: Recommend one product you really use that helps {audience} with {problem}, and explain who it is not right for.

stageHints.idea: Learn the rules and save the disclosure template for later.
stageHints.started: Add one affiliate link to the video where it fits best.
stageHints.some_traction: Add links to your top videos and track clicks.
stageHints.already_earning: Audit all existing links and disclosures for accuracy.

plan.missionTitle: Publish a video that genuinely helps viewers choose or use a tool.
plan.goal: Video 5 is live with an honest recommendation.

tasks.title: Script an honest review or tutorial
tasks.description: Cover who it is for, who it is not for and what you wish you knew first.

tasks.title: Record and edit
tasks.description: Show the product in use instead of reading features.

tasks.title: Add the disclosure
tasks.description: Mention the affiliate link in the video and the description.

tasks.title: Publish
tasks.description: Publish and pin a comment answering a common question about it.

plan.nicheHint: Show how the product helps {audience} with {problem} in real use, including limits.

stageHints.idea: Make a tutorial on a free tool instead if you have nothing to recommend yet.
stageHints.started: Publish your first honest recommendation video.

resources.title: Channel Setup Checklist
resources.description: Everything a new visitor needs to understand your channel in five seconds. Work through it once, then revisit it monthly.

sections.heading: Basics
body: Channel name: short, easy to spell and easy to say out loud.
Profile picture: your face or a simple logo that reads at small size.
Handle: matches your channel name as closely as possible.

sections.heading: Banner
body: Use Canva's free YouTube banner template.
Put your promise in large text inside the safe area so it shows on phones.
Add your upload rhythm, such as "New videos every Thursday".

sections.heading: About section
body: Line 1: who the channel is for.
Line 2: what they will learn or get.
Line 3: how often you upload and a contact email if you want brand messages.

sections.heading: Final check
body: Open your channel in the YouTube app on your phone.
Ask a friend what your channel is about after five seconds.
Fix anything they could not tell you.

resources.title: Audience Research Worksheet
resources.description: A simple worksheet to collect real questions from search, comments and Google Trends before you choose topics.

sections.heading: Search autocomplete
body: Type your topic into YouTube search and save every suggestion.
Add "how to", "why", "best", "vs" and "for beginners" after your topic.
Try each letter of the alphabet after your topic for more suggestions.

sections.heading: Comments on similar channels
body: Pick five channels close to your size in your topic.
Read comments on their three most recent videos.
Copy questions, complaints and requests in the viewer's exact words.

sections.heading: Google Trends
body: Set the filter to YouTube Search and the range to 12 months.
Compare up to five topic phrases.
Mark each as steady, rising or seasonal.

sections.heading: Score and choose
body: Score each topic 0 to 3 for interest, your knowledge and ease of filming.
Keep your top five topics as channel pillars.
Health, finance or legal topic? Plan to frame videos as education, not personal advice.

resources.title: Idea Bank Template
resources.description: A living list of video ideas so you never start a filming day without a plan. Aim for 20 ideas and add new ones weekly.

sections.heading: Columns
body: Idea: one question for one viewer.
Working title: the title a viewer would click.
Source: autocomplete, comment, Trends or your own experience.
Status: idea, scripted, recorded, published.

sections.heading: Good idea test
body: Does it answer one specific question?
Could you film it this week with what you have?
Have you seen people ask for it more than once?

sections.heading: Weekly habit
body: Copy new questions from your comments every week.
Add follow-up ideas for your best-performing videos.
Move finished ideas to a published list with the link.

resources.title: Video Script Template
resources.description: A four-part script structure that works in any niche: hook, promise, content and call to action.

sections.heading: Hook (first 15 to 30 seconds)
body: Question: "Why does [common problem] keep happening?"
Result: "Here is how I [result] using [simple method]."
Mistake: "Most beginners make this mistake with [topic]."

sections.heading: Promise
body: "By the end of this video you will know [specific outcome]."
Keep it to one sentence and make it something the video actually delivers.

sections.heading: Content
body: Three to five points, each with an example or demonstration.
Short spoken sentences. Read it out loud and cut anything you stumble on.
Add a quick recap before the end.

sections.heading: Call to action and sensitive topics
body: Ask for one thing: watch a related video, comment a question or subscribe.
Health, finance or legal topics: say the video is educational, add a short disclaimer and suggest viewers consult a qualified professional for their situation.

resources.title: Phone Recording Checklist
resources.description: Get clean video and audio on a phone with no extra equipment. Run through it before every recording.

sections.heading: Light
body: Face a window during the day.
Never sit with a bright window behind you.
Turn off mixed-color overhead lights if they make your face look odd.

sections.heading: Audio
body: Pick the quietest room with soft surfaces like curtains or a bed.
Close windows and turn off fans.
Stay close to the phone or use wired earphones with a mic.

sections.heading: Camera
body: Clean the lens.
Use the back camera if you can; it is usually better quality.
Put the phone at eye level and use a stack of books if you have no tripod.

sections.heading: Before you hit record
body: Record a 20-second test and listen with headphones.
Turn on Do Not Disturb.
Check you have enough storage and battery.

resources.title: Title and Thumbnail Checklist
resources.description: Package each video so the right viewers want to click, without misleading anyone.

sections.heading: Title
body: Write ten options, then choose the clearest.
Use the words your viewers use in search.
Promise a result the video actually delivers.

sections.heading: Thumbnail
body: One subject, one feeling, high contrast.
Three words or fewer of text, and not the same words as the title.
Check it at phone size next to other videos in your topic.

sections.heading: Before publishing
body: Do the title and thumbnail tell one story together?
Would a viewer feel the video matched what they clicked?
Is the first line of the description a clear summary?

resources.title: Analytics Review Guide
resources.description: A plain-English guide to the YouTube Studio numbers that matter early, and how to turn them into decisions.

sections.heading: Where to look
body: YouTube Studio > Analytics for the channel view.
Click a single video, then Analytics, for its own numbers.
Use the Content, Audience and Reach tabs.

sections.heading: What each number means
body: Impressions click-through rate: how often people who saw your thumbnail clicked.
Average view duration and retention: how long people stayed and where they left.
Traffic sources: search, browse, Shorts feed, suggested or external.
Returning viewers: people who came back after watching before.

sections.heading: How to compare fairly
body: Compare your own videos to each other, not to other channels.
Compare over the same time window, such as the first 7 days.
Small numbers still show patterns, but do not overreact to one video.

sections.heading: Turn it into decisions
body: Low clicks: improve the title and thumbnail.
Early drop in retention: tighten the hook and opening.
Write one thing to repeat, one to stop and one experiment.

resources.title: Publishing Schedule Planner
resources.description: Plan a cadence you can keep and assign production steps to real dates.

sections.heading: Estimate your time
body: Write how long each step took on your last video: script, record, edit, package.
Add them up and add a buffer of about a third.
That total is your real time per video.

sections.heading: Pick a cadence
body: Light: one long video every two weeks plus one Short a week.
Steady: one long video a week plus two Shorts.
Choose the one you could keep during a busy week.

sections.heading: Monthly calendar
body: Assign one idea from your bank to each publish date.
Block script, record and edit days before each date.
Plan at least one Short from each long video and leave one buffer week.

resources.title: Affiliate Disclosure and Link Guide
resources.description: How to use affiliate links honestly, disclose them clearly and keep viewer trust.

sections.heading: Before you add a link
body: Only recommend products you have used yourself.
Read the affiliate program's rules, including where links may be shared.
Check that the product genuinely helps the audience of that video.

sections.heading: How to disclose
body: Say it in the video near the mention: "The link below is an affiliate link."
Add a plain line in the description above or next to the link.
If the video includes paid promotion, tick the paid promotion setting in YouTube Studio.
Follow the advertising disclosure rules in your country.

sections.heading: Sensitive topics
body: Health, finance or legal products: stay educational and share your own experience only.
Do not make medical, financial or legal claims or promise results.
Suggest viewers consult a qualified professional for their situation.

sections.heading: Track and maintain
body: Use the program's dashboard to see clicks.
Check links every month and remove dead ones.
Note which videos drive clicks so you plan more like them.

resources.title: Media Kit Template
resources.description: A one-page media kit that shows brands who your audience is and what your channel covers, using real numbers only.

sections.heading: Header
body: Channel name, handle and channel promise.
One sentence about who you are and why you make these videos.
Contact email.

sections.heading: Audience snapshot
body: Who watches: main age ranges, top countries and interests, from YouTube Studio's Audience tab.
Recent averages: views per video and average view duration over the last 28 or 90 days.
Returning viewers and subscribers gained in that period.

sections.heading: Content and fit
body: Your three best videos with links.
Types of partnerships you offer, such as a dedicated video or an integrated mention.
Brands and products you will not promote.

text.youtube_owned:
Your next video should answer a question your audience is already asking.

1. Open your idea bank and look for questions you saw more than once.
2. If it is thin, type your topic into YouTube search and note the autocomplete suggestions.
3. Read comments on three similar small channels and copy repeat questions.

Next step: pick one question and write a working title in the viewer's own words.

followUps: How do I use search autocomplete?
Can you help me write a working title?
How many ideas should I have?

text.youtube_owned:
Low views on a new channel are normal and they usually come down to packaging or topic, not your worth as a creator.

Check two numbers in YouTube Studio: impressions and click-through rate. Few impressions means the topic may not be searched much yet; low click-through means the title and thumbnail need work.

Next step: pick your weakest video, write ten new titles and simplify the thumbnail, then compare in a week.

followUps: What is a good click-through rate?
How do I improve my thumbnail?
Should I delete low-view videos?

text.youtube_owned:
Subscribers follow when a viewer expects more videos they want. One video rarely does it; a clear promise and related videos do.

Make sure your banner and About text say who the channel is for, and link each video to a related one with end screens.

Next step: plan a follow-up to your best video so new viewers have a reason to stay.

followUps: How do I add end screens?
What should my channel promise be?
Should I ask people to subscribe?

text.youtube_owned:
If viewers leave early, the opening is the first thing to fix.

Start with the problem in the viewer's words, then promise a clear result in one sentence. Cut greetings and long intros before the hook.

Next step: open the retention graph of your last video, find where the biggest early drop happens and rewrite that part for your next script.

followUps: Can you write three hooks for my next video?
How do I read the retention graph?
How long should my intro be?

text.youtube_owned:
Title and thumbnail work as one message. The title says the result; the thumbnail shows the feeling or the subject.

Write ten titles in your audience's words and choose the clearest. Keep the thumbnail to one subject and three words or fewer, then check it at phone size next to other videos.

Next step: tell me your video topic and I will help you draft ten titles.

followUps: How do I make a thumbnail in Canva?

Consistency means a rhythm you can keep, not posting every day.

Estimate how long your last video really took, then choose a cadence that fits your busiest week, such as one long video every two weeks plus a Short. Batch two scripts at once so one bad week does not break it.

Almost everyone feels awkward on camera at first, and it fades with repetition.

You can start without showing your face: screen recordings, hands-on demos or voiceover over b-roll all work in many niches. If you do show your face, record in short sections and remember you can cut every mistake.

Edit in this order: cut silences and mistakes, tighten the opening, add captions, then extras. Save your project as a template so next time starts faster.

Compare your own videos to each other over the same time window, not to other channels. Clicks point to packaging; early drop-off points to the hook.

Channel income usually takes months, and ads are often not the first source.

Check the current eligibility requirements in YouTube Studio > Earn, since they change. Meanwhile, the realistic first attempts are an affiliate link for something you really use, being sponsorship-ready with a simple media kit, or validating a small digital product idea.

Affiliate links work best when you recommend something you actually use and explain who it is for and who it is not for.

Disclose it in the video and the description, tick the paid promotion setting when it applies, and follow the advertising rules in your country. In health, finance or legal topics, stay educational and avoid professional claims.

Brands look for a clear audience fit more than big numbers.

Build a one-page media kit with your channel promise, an audience snapshot from YouTube Studio, your best three videos and a contact email. Use real numbers only and decide what you will not promote.

Feeling tired is a sign your schedule is too heavy, not that you are failing.

Slow your cadence to something you could keep for a year, batch when you have energy and plan rest days. A slower channel that keeps going beats a fast one that stops.
